summary: Direction faithfully extracted, but the NODE is wrong. 3 of 4 papers report 'Erysipelotrichaceae UCG-003', an uncultured genus-level SILVA placeholder INSIDE the family, which taxonomy.py folded onto the family taxid. The 4th names the family but attributes the change to a member (Eubacterium biforme). No paper measures the family aggregate, so our family-level 'depleted' is an aggregation artifact. The curated databases record the family enriched in PD; both can be true simultaneously.
quote: HC samples consistently exhibited higher relative abundances of SCFA-producing genera such as Blautia, Fusicatenibacter, and Erysipelotrichaceae UCG-003.
action: Do not fold rank placeholders into their parent. Split UCG-003 into its own node.

summary: Three independent papers, explicit and quantitative. One of them names the contradicting prior study itself.
quote: The abundance of Dorea was greatly lower in patients with cognitive impairment than that in normal controls (mean, AD vs. MCI vs. NC: 0.17% vs. 0.13% vs. 0.54%, p < 0.01)
action: Keep. The source paper states 'which was contrary to Liu's findings (Liu et al., 2019)' — the disagreement is real and already acknowledged in the literature.

summary: Not a contradiction. Both our papers are SALIVA/oral microbiome studies in PD with dementia; the curated records are gut. Our edge does not carry body site, so an oral finding and a gut finding collide on one node.
quote: SAL1, enriched in PDD patients, was increased in pathobionts such as Streptococcus, Rothia and Veillonella and showed an enrichment for proline biosynthesis.
action: Add body site to the edge key, or restrict the graph to stool.

summary: Paper 1 is explicit and unconditional. Paper 2's support is weaker and CONDITIONAL — the reduction is female-specific — which our unconditional edge does not record.
quote: The NPD group presented higher levels of Bulleidia, Turicibacter, and Adlercreutzia and lower levels of Streptococcus, Ruminococcus, and Paraprevotella compared to the HCs.
action: Keep, but note the second paper's effect is sex-conditional; the edge over-claims generality.

summary: Source paper is not in relation_sentences.json (which covers only the original 250), so no sentence is retrievable here.
action: Re-run the sentence filter over the full 326-paper corpus, then adjudicate.

summary: Correctly extracted. Note the contrast is iRBD and PD-with-RBD versus controls, i.e. a PD subgroup rather than PD at large.
quote: 4 genera (Aerococcus, Eubacterium, Gordonibacter and Stenotrophomonas) were found consistently increased while 3 genera (Butyricicoccus, Faecalibacterium and Haemophilus) were found consistently decreased in iRBD and PD with RBD group.
action: Keep; flag as an RBD-subgroup finding.

summary: Correctly extracted from a PDD-prediction feature list.
quote: The decrease in beneficial bacteria such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Roseburia faecis, Roseburia inulinivorans, Eubacterium rectale in the gut ... were the most important features in predicting PDD
action: Keep. Single paper against single records on both sides — low evidence all round.

summary: The only sentence naming the taxon reports a CORRELATION WITH DISEASE STAGE, not a case-vs-control contrast, and states no direction at all. The 'depleted' direction was manufactured. The curated databases are more likely right here.
quote: On genus level, in addition to Faecalibacterium, also Bacteroides, Clostridium, Phascolarctobacterium, Coprococcus, Odoribacter were correlated with disease stage.
action: DROP this edge. Correlation-with-severity is not enrichment vs healthy controls.

summary: Correctly extracted, and the paper explicitly frames itself as disagreeing with the studies the databases curate. Caveat: it calls these 'non-abundant genera'.
quote: Different from Vogt's and Liu's studies, we found that such non-abundant genera as Collinsella, Enterococcus, Olsenella, Eubacterium, Christensenella, Anaerotruncus, and Halomonas were also enriched in AD-associated fecal microbiota
action: Keep; low-abundance taxon, weak on both sides.

summary: No retrievable text. Sole source is the same saliva metaproteogenomic paper behind pair 3, so a body-site mismatch is the likely explanation.
action: Treat as probable body-site mismatch; confirm after re-running the filter on the full corpus.

summary: The best-documented dispute of the fourteen. Correctly extracted, large effect, and the paper identifies the contradicting study AND proposes a mechanism for the discrepancy.
quote: the genus Dialister has previously been shown to have a higher relative abundance in PD patients in a Southern China population [50], which may reflect dietary or other geographical differences.
action: Keep. This is what a legitimately contested edge looks like.

summary: Correctly extracted from an LEfSe comparison against healthy controls.
quote: The mean abundances of the genera Lactobacillus, Streptococcus, Enterobacter, Citrobacter, Hungatella, Erysipelatoclostridium, and Veillonella were higher in the HC group than in the OPD group

summary: Correctly extracted; two sentences in the same paper agree.
quote: The NPD group presented higher levels of Bulleidia, Turicibacter, and Adlercreutzia ... compared to the HCs.

HCs had a slightly (but significantly) lower abundance of Bulleidia, Turicibacter, and Adlercreutzia and higher levels of Streptococcus, Ruminococcus, Paraprevotella, 7N15, and Acidaminococcus than the NPD group
